**Observations from test image:**
- Soybean leaf (upper surface view)
- Diffuse interveinal chlorosis/yellowing — areas between veins are pale yellow-green
- Major veins remain noticeably greener than surrounding tissue
- Scattered small reddish-brown spots/necrotic flecks throughout the interveinal zones
- No discrete circular lesions with defined borders

**Reasoning:**
- The hallmark pattern of **interveinal chlorosis with veins remaining green** strongly points to Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS)
- SDS description: "scattered yellow spots between leaf veins... midvein and major lateral veins remain green"
- The small reddish-brown flecks represent early necrosis developing within the chlorotic areas — consistent with early-to-mid stage SDS
- The SDS reference collage confirms this pattern (upper right panel shows the same interveinal yellow/green mosaic)
- Septoria brown spot would show more discrete dark brown spots without the interveinal chlorosis pattern; Soybean Vein Necrosis would show necrosis *along* veins rather than *between* them
